reason: The hypothesis directly restates the finding from P5 and P7 that low-temperature aging of AlCoFeNi produces a B2+BCC phase decomposition which increases coercivity, and proposes the same intervention (aging) on the same alloy system. The mechanism of domain wall pinning by precipitates is taken from P1, P5, P7, and P9, and the idea of controlling precipitate size to tune coercivity is explicitly suggested as future work in P9 and P29. The hypothesis adds only a generic specification of aging time and temperature, which is a minor variation of the conditions already studied.
